newsitem.title: USA: No separate peace talks with N.Korea - U.S.
newsitem.headline: No separate peace talks with N.Korea - U.S.

text.p: The United States on Friday reassured South Korea that it would not hold separate peace talks with North Korea and said the threat from Pyongyang had not grown despite a submarine incursion into the South.

"During the past year the military threat posed by North Korea has not increased and therefore that does not provide a basis for making an increase in U.S. forces (in the South)," Defence Secretary William Perry told reporters.
He said at a joint news conference with new South Korean Defence Minister South Kim Dong-jin that 37,000 U.S. troops would remain in South Korea on a high state of alert.
Perry and Kim also said after two days of annual bilateral talks that "separate negotiations between the United States and North Korea on peace-related issues cannot be considered."

"Both agreed that South and North Korea should take the lead in the search for a permanent peace arrangement" on the peninsula, where a 1953 armistice ended the Korean War, according to a joint communique on the talks.

Kim and Perry again condemned the September incursion by a North Korean submarine into South Korean waters but said Washington and Seoul would press for final peace and urge the North to complete an agreement under which less threatening nuclear reactors would be built in the North.

They urged Pyongyang to open a serious dialogue with Seoul and to enter into four-way talks with the United States, South Korea and China to turn the armistice that ended the 1950-53 Korean War into permanent peace.

The four-way talks were proposed this year by President Bill Clinton and South Korea's President Kim Young-sam. North Korea, which wants to isolate its hated foe in the South with bilateral talks with Washington, has not accepted.

The Shark-class North Korean submarine ran aground off Kangnung, South Korea, on Sept. 17 as it tried to pick up three spies it had landed two days earlier, according to the only North Korean captured alive from the vessel.
Twenty-six North Koreans involved in the submarine mission fled to the South Korean hills. Twenty-two have been shot dead and a hunt is under way for three missing intruders.
Partly to defuse criticism and to signal a tougher defence posture, President Kim ordered a sweeping reshuffle of the military top brass and sacked Defence Minister Lee Yang-ho.

Friday's communique said the United States and South Korea would continue discussing the possible resumption of annual "Team Spirit" military exercises, which the North has called a preparation for war. "We haven't reached any conclusion on this," Minister Kim said. "If there is any decision, it will be made at the end of this year or early next year."
